## ✨ Highlights

- 🔒 **HAProxy security update, every branch**: HAProxy 3.4.8, 3.2.27
  and 3.0.31 fix the same four vulnerabilities rated high in all three -
  two in HTTP/2, one in buffer handling, one in the cache. Update every
  node, whatever HAProxy branch its image has.

Everything else is as in v2026.11.19-2.

## 🔒 Security

- **HAProxy 3.4 3.4.7 → 3.4.8** (nodes on HAProxy 3.4 - the default HAProxy branch, or pinned to it):
  - 🟠 high [haproxy-29ba69b](https://git.haproxy.org/?p=haproxy-3.4.git;a=commitdiff;h=29ba69b) - BUG/MAJOR: mux-h2: split absolute URIs like the HTTP analysers do on output;
  - 🟠 high [haproxy-68abc77](https://git.haproxy.org/?p=haproxy-3.4.git;a=commitdiff;h=68abc77) - BUG/MAJOR: mux-h2: fail on impossible data transfers in rcv_buf();
  - 🟠 high [haproxy-6e9920e](https://git.haproxy.org/?p=haproxy-3.4.git;a=commitdiff;h=6e9920e) - BUG/MAJOR: buf: make the shift distance check less strict in b_move();
  - 🟠 high [haproxy-7db4355](https://git.haproxy.org/?p=haproxy-3.4.git;a=commitdiff;h=7db4355) - BUG/MAJOR: cache: do not mix variants varying on different headers;
  - 7 more don't apply (Janus's HAProxy is built without QUIC/HTTP/3); 83 other bug fixes.
- **HAProxy 3.2 3.2.26 → 3.2.27** (nodes pinned to HAProxy 3.2):
  - 🟠 high [haproxy-7a12780](https://git.haproxy.org/?p=haproxy-3.2.git;a=commitdiff;h=7a12780) - BUG/MAJOR: mux-h2: split absolute URIs like the HTTP analysers do on output;
  - 🟠 high [haproxy-be6e654](https://git.haproxy.org/?p=haproxy-3.2.git;a=commitdiff;h=be6e654) - BUG/MAJOR: mux-h2: fail on impossible data transfers in rcv_buf();
  - 🟠 high [haproxy-80c92e3](https://git.haproxy.org/?p=haproxy-3.2.git;a=commitdiff;h=80c92e3) - BUG/MAJOR: buf: make the shift distance check less strict in b_move();
  - 🟠 high [haproxy-045265a](https://git.haproxy.org/?p=haproxy-3.2.git;a=commitdiff;h=045265a) - BUG/MAJOR: cache: do not mix variants varying on different headers;
  - 6 more don't apply (Janus's HAProxy is built without QUIC/HTTP/3); 61 other bug fixes.
- **HAProxy 3.0 3.0.30 → 3.0.31** (nodes pinned to HAProxy 3.0):
  - 🟠 high [haproxy-8ad5dc8](https://git.haproxy.org/?p=haproxy-3.0.git;a=commitdiff;h=8ad5dc8) - BUG/MAJOR: mux-h2: split absolute URIs like the HTTP analysers do on output;
  - 🟠 high [haproxy-79d7f98](https://git.haproxy.org/?p=haproxy-3.0.git;a=commitdiff;h=79d7f98) - BUG/MAJOR: mux-h2: fail on impossible data transfers in rcv_buf();
  - 🟠 high [haproxy-45c3b89](https://git.haproxy.org/?p=haproxy-3.0.git;a=commitdiff;h=45c3b89) - BUG/MAJOR: buf: make the shift distance check less strict in b_move();
  - 🟠 high [haproxy-c7acd97](https://git.haproxy.org/?p=haproxy-3.0.git;a=commitdiff;h=c7acd97) - BUG/MAJOR: cache: do not mix variants varying on different headers;
  - 5 more don't apply (Janus's HAProxy is built without QUIC/HTTP/3); 55 other bug fixes.

What they mean for a node:

- **HTTP/2 to the servers** (a `server` line with `proto h2`, or `alpn
  h2` negotiated): a request whose URI is in absolute form
  (`GET http://host/path`) could be checked against one host and path
  by the configuration's rules, then sent to the server with another -
  host and path rules could be bypassed.
- **HTTP/2 data transfers**: a client could leave a stream stuck in
  HAProxy for good, holding what it had taken.
- **Buffer moves**: traffic could make HAProxy stop on one of its own
  internal checks. janusd starts it again, but every connection it held
  is cut.
- **The cache with `process-vary on`** (not the default): any client
  could store a variant of a response that the cache then served to
  every other client, whatever their `Origin` or `Referer` - CORS checks
  broken for the legitimate sites, or contents mixed between referrers.

The Controller's update badge (🔒) shows on every node until it runs
this release: each HAProxy branch has fixes.

## 🔗 Clusters

- **Peers and certificates**: the new versions also fix how `peers`
  sections schedule their synchronisation and send their updates, and a
  `commit ssl cert` that is interrupted - what a cluster uses to share
  its stick tables and to renew its members' certificates without a
  reload. Clusters of nodes on each branch were tested: tables
  replicated and learnt back, a member's certificate renewed at runtime.

## 📖 Docs

- **[HAProxy's configuration on Janus](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/haproxy-config.md)**:
  `ssl-provider-path` joins the keywords the node refuses (AWS-LC loads
  no OpenSSL 3 provider), as HAProxy 3.4.8's own documentation now says.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **`cache-use` or `cache-store` in a `defaults` section**: HAProxy now
  refuses them (`'cache-use' rules are not supported in a defaults
  section`), in every branch. Such rules never worked there - HAProxy
  crashed, or cached nothing - so move them into the frontends or
  backends that use the cache **before** updating: a node whose
  configuration still has them can't start HAProxy on the new release.
  With `-wait-for-health` - on by default on the Controller's Update
  page - the node goes back to its previous slot by itself. To check
  a node: `janusctl -n NODE haproxy get-config`, and look at its
  `defaults` sections.
- **Nodes**: the usual A/B update - a node keeps its HAProxy branch. A
  custom image (the factory) of this release has the new HAProxy of its
  branch.
- **The Controller, janusctl, the Terraform provider**: nothing changed
  beyond the version.
